research_notes: Initial research 2026-10-01. OpenAustralia.org reproduction of the 2018 Senate first speech supplies earlier Commonwealth and UK council employment and explicit part-time history. Own 2019 House speech supplies paid Big W work. Frozen three occupations preserved with documentary conflicts flagged.

Follow-up: precise Big W and Commonwealth dates, role titles, substantive hours and any gaps; Slough Council appointment/payroll history and UK travel dates; original ACT appointment/cessation evidence to resolve 2004 versus 2005 transition. No 1990s year is invented from broad wording.

Explicit workload caveat: he said both partners worked part time after returning from the UK. Employer, dates and fraction are unallocated. Do not mark every later role part-time, nor treat unallocated periods as full-time. Union employer accommodated family commitments; no specific leave period established.

Follow-up: AFPA/Professionals Australia exact transitions, different union titles and any breaks; whether any further paid jobs existed. Excluded union roles still require employment-history coverage. Missing full-time evidence is not zero.

Searched own biographies, both first speeches, union publications, government bargaining and stakeholder records, historical report searches, public professional index and workload queries. No identity-safe employer annual report with individual hours found. Separate ASU and AMWU officials named David Smith, the former Governor-General secretary, UK MP and other professionals excluded; speech explicitly warns of union namesakes.

Recovered source access gaps: linked Parlinfo Hansard (403) Forbidden; AFPA magazine (400) Content length is too large: 11033887; LinkedIn direct (999) Unknown Status Code. Public indexed material and first-person speech reproduction used transparently, without bypass. Exact dates remain uncertain and headline totals null.

Follow-up2026-10-02: correct public professional profile supplies Slough council2001–2002 and service-improvement responsibilities; AFPA2004–2007 senior industrial officer description supports earlier transition but does not resolve frozen2005manager start. No title from another entry assigned to council.

Targeted profile/Slough/AFPA searches supplied year-level boundaries only. PFA2005–06 report index naming David Smith(AFPA) is a corroboration lead, not additional full-time evidence. No exact Commonwealth/BigW dates, hours or employer allocation of post-UK part-time arrangements found. Next useful evidence: original Slough appointment, ACT separation and AFPA appointment/promotion records.

Follow-up 2026-10-04: Smith's own Adult Age = Adult Wage page explicitly calls the Woden Big W role his first job. This strengthens the known start of paid work and argues against inserting an undocumented earlier employer, but provides no date or workload evidence; exact school-age boundaries and employment status remain unknown.
